findings.statement: The three later base_02 false NOT_FLAT claims have different exact defects. Arm5 70B records sr2*s=r, but the table gives r2 and the final product e. Arm5 SBA replaces edge 2,3->1,3=s with sr, so it computes a changed input. Arm6 SBA records r*sr=s, but the table gives sr2 and final product e. A classification failure can therefore reflect arithmetic or instance-binding errors even when a scratchpad appears explicit.
findings.recommended_action: Reuse these three error classes as public checker controls with new independently encoded tasks. Verify edge binding and every ordered multiplication; do not treat scratchpad length as correctness or reuse these known answers as a sealed benchmark.

findings.statement: Recorded C017 acceptance counts are 0/5,0/5,3/5,3/5,4/5. The first two arms retain no actual certificate payloads; later arms add canonical paths, step rules and, in arm6, harness-listed active plaquettes/cycle paths. Two later torus attempts retain PARSE_ERROR and only incomplete raw prefixes. These records cannot isolate causal prompt/learning effects, reconstruct all attempts or establish unaided capability.
findings.recommended_action: Keep assistance, missingness, parse failure and certificate acceptance as separate fields; design any future comparison with independently selected cases, fixed assistance and retained complete execution inputs.
